> LLM-generated review from https://github.com/canonical/maas-code-reviewer.
> Intended to assist a human reviewer, not replace one — suggestions may be
> incorrect, please verify before acting.


Solid, well-tested port of the legacy `maasserver.dhcp` host/subnet/interface selection into the v3 service layer; behavior (relay handling, interface preference, NTP/space keys, DNS fallbacks, host reservation dedupe) tracks the Django implementation closely, and all new SQL goes through Clause/QuerySpec so there are no injection concerns.

Main concerns, in priority order:
1. Query cost on what will be a per-rack, frequently-refreshed path. `_get_best_interface_with_ip_on_vlan` does `1 + |interfaces| + |IPs|` round-trips per subnet, is invoked again from `_get_ip_address_for_rack_controller` for the HA peer (re-fetching peer interfaces/NTP per subnet), host reservations do a `get_for_ip` and a node lookup per host, and `_get_alt_region_ips_for_dns` queries per (server, region). Legacy prefetched all of this in a handful of queries. Batch/group these or the endpoint will be slow on racks with many interfaces/hosts.
2. `assert` on DB-derived values (`_make_interface_hostname`, `_get_best_interface_with_ip_on_vlan`, `_get_ntp_servers_for_rack`, `_get_boot_rack_controller_ips`) turns unexpected data into a bare `AssertionError`/500 and disappears under `python -O`. `_make_interface_hostname` is the concrete case: `NodeClauseFactory.with_node_config_id` matches only the node's *current* config, while `get_for_ip` returns any linked interface (non-current `NodeConfig`s exist), so the lookup can legitimately return `None` where the legacy code used `interface.node_config.node.hostname`.
3. `configured_ip_versions` is applied only after every per-subnet computation, so `_get_ha_config`/DNS/NTP run (and can raise) for families the result is about to drop.
4. `StaticIPAddressClauseFactory.with_interface_enabled` references `InterfaceTable` without declaring joins; it is only correct because `get_for_nodes` happens to join that table. Any other repository method would silently cross-join.

Minor: empty-string `gateway_ip` sentinel in `SubnetData`, duplicated top-level `ntp_servers` computation, and a couple of tests that assert exact `QuerySpec` clause objects (e.g. `test_only_includes_owned_dhcp_vlans_and_managed_subnets`) rather than observable results, which re-pins implementation.

src/maasservicelayer/db/repositories/sta.107: `with_interface_enabled` filters on `InterfaceTable` but, unlike `with_interface_ids` below, declares no `joins`. It only works today because `StaticIPAddressRepository.get_for_nodes` happens to join `InterfaceIPAddressTable`/`InterfaceTable`; used with `get_many`/`get_one`/`get_by_id` this silently becomes a cartesian join (rows multiplied, no error). Add the same `joins=[...]` as `with_interface_ids` — `QuerySpec._enrich_select_stmt` skips joins already present, so `get_for_nodes` is unaffected.

src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.344: The family filter runs only after all per-subnet work. That wastes the `_get_dhcp_host_reservations` queries (executed for every managed subnet at lines 250-259), the DNS resolution in `_get_default_dns_servers_for_subnet`, and the HA/NTP lookups — and it can abort on data that is then discarded: for a dual-stack HA VLAN where the controllers have no address in one family, `_get_ha_config` (line 271) raises before that family is dropped here. Derive `configured_ip_versions` from the interfaces first and skip those subnets inside the loop.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.370: This recomputes exactly the `default_dns_servers` expression from lines 238-245 (same `rack_ips`, same subnet filter, same dedupe). Compute it once (or extract a helper) so the intent — global NTP servers are the rack's IPs when `ntp_external_only` is unset — is explicit and the two copies cannot drift.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.422: Per-interface/per-IP N+1: one `get_for_interfaces` call per interface, plus a `get_by_id` and a `get_many` (dynamic-range count) per IP, for every subnet. `_get_ip_address_for_rack_controller` then repeats all of this for the HA peer, re-fetching `_get_rack_interfaces(peer)` for each subnet without caching. On a rack with M interfaces and P addresses across H subnets this is O(H × M × P) round-trips on a frequently-called path; legacy prefetched it. Fetch IPs for all rack interfaces in one query, index by interface/subnet, count dynamic ranges once per subnet outside the IP loop, and cache interfaces/NTP per rack id.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.432: `assert ip_subnet is not None` (same pattern in `_get_ntp_servers_for_rack`, `_get_boot_rack_controller_ips`, `_make_interface_hostname`) raises a bare `AssertionError` → 500 on unexpected data and is stripped under `python -O`, after which `ip_subnet.id` below fails with `AttributeError`. Prefer explicit handling (skip or raise a catalogued exception) for values coming from the database.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.592: Host reservation building is another N+1: `get_for_ip` per IP, `get_parents` per bond, and a node lookup per emitted host inside `_make_interface_hostname`. For a subnet with many reservations this dominates the request. Collect the IP ids/interfaces in bulk (the legacy implementation prefetched `interface_set` and parents in a single query) and cache node lookups by `node_config_id`.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.666: `NodeClauseFactory.with_node_config_id` filters on `Node.current_config_id`, but `interfaces_service.get_for_ip` returns interfaces linked to any node config (old `NodeConfig` rows survive config duplication, and IP links are not duplicated onto the new config). If the interface belongs to a non-current config this returns `None` and the `assert` raises → 500 for the whole rack's DHCP payload; the legacy code used `interface.node_config.node.hostname` and worked for any config. Handle `None` (fall back to `unknown-<id>-<name>`) or add a lookup that resolves the node from `node_config_id` directly.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.797: The `seen_regions` guard is evaluated after the query at line 781, so the region query is still issued for entries that will be skipped immediately. Move the check above the query (and consider caching `find_best_subnet_for_ip` results) — this loop runs per resolved DNS server × per region.

src/maasservicelayer/models/dhcp.py.45: `gateway_ip: str` uses `""` as the no-gateway sentinel (see the service at lines 320-322), while `Subnet.gateway_ip` is `IPvAnyAddress | None`. The empty-string sentinel forces every consumer to special-case it; `str | None` is cleaner and lossless.
